spatial_and_orientation_analysis: In both supplied images a bed is left of a white cubby shelf and a chair occupies the foreground; the candidate places a dark vertical slab on the right. The reference fills the frame with a close interior view, while the candidate shows wall tops, room exterior and substantially more floor; the bed and shelf project smaller and with different perspective. This is a coupled camera/layout/proportion discrepancy, not a measured 3D error. Evidence: supplied reference and candidate images; final_source/build.py:17-41,64-83.

The bed's long axis, headboard, and chair back provide partial orientation cues, but chair facing and hidden structural relationships are not uniquely recoverable from the reference. The right reference object is a GT door instance while the student named its slab wardrobe; a hinge, jamb and opening are not established by that slab. Evidence: reference_instance_statistics.json:145-160,338-352; original object_inventory.jsonl:101-110; final_source/build.py:64-78.
appearance_and_resource_analysis: The reference has bright, localized lamp illumination, visible wood grain and a textured mattress. The delivered image has more uniform muted illumination, a plain brown bedside top and smooth mattress. These are visual observations, not proof of isolated material or lighting effects. Evidence: supplied reference and candidate images; final_source/build.py:6-8,38,43,57-63,79-81.

The executed source creates Principled materials with constant base color, roughness and metallic inputs and binds them via mesh material slots; it does not construct image textures, UV mappings or the library's object-coordinate noise chain. Thus no texture image path, packed texture resource, grain mapping direction or frequency is evidenced by this source. Evidence: final_source/build.py:6-16,23-26,43,57-63; available_library/reconstruct.py:88-114. The name white quilted mattress is not proof of quilting geometry or texture. The scene is constructed as objects, not a full-reference image plane (final_source/build.py:17-87).
geometry_analysis: The shelf consists of two sides, four vertical dividers and five horizontal boards, creating five columns and four rows; reference shelf appearance differs in its grid. The chair is a separate ellipsoid seat, subdivided/solidified back and four legs, unlike the more continuous visible reference silhouette. Evidence: final_source/build.py:28-32,64-74; supplied images; original object_inventory.jsonl:33-43,101-106.

The student scene contains two floor lamps but the right one is largely obscured by the dark slab in the final image, unlike the prominent right reference lamp. AABB bounds are coarse and do not verify physical contacts or connectivity. Evidence: final_source/build.py:57-63,78; original object_inventory.jsonl:93-100,110; supplied images.
